Today Apple announced three new flagship iPhone models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the foldable iPhone Duo. Here's an overview of the key differences between each model.

Design and Dimensions: Foldable vs Traditional

This is the most obvious difference, but it's still worth mentioning. The iPhone Duo features a completely different design, as it's a foldable device. The iPhone 18 Pro offers the traditional iPhone experience.

If you've never used a foldable device, it's hard to explain how the two models feel in actual use. But generally speaking, the iPhone Duo combines the iPhone and iPad into one. However, its screen shape and size are different from traditional iPhones, so it may take some time to get used to.

Here's a size comparison of each model:

The iPhone Duo appears thinner than the iPhone 18 Pro Max, but it's actually slightly heavier.

Display: Dual Screens vs Single Screen, Different Sizes

The iPhone Duo features two displays: a 5.4-inch outer screen and a 7.6-inch foldable screen.

The iPhone 18 Pro comes in either a 6.3-inch standard version or a 6.9-inch Pro Max version.

Therefore, the iPhone Duo offers the experience of a "compact iPhone" while providing a larger inner screen than the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

The iPhone Duo's foldable screen uses a nano-texture coating, a first for the iPhone.

Camera: The iPhone 18 Pro Is Clearly Superior

The camera is one of the most important features of the iPhone, and in this regard, the iPhone 18 Pro clearly wins.

The iPhone 18 Pro features a new 48-megapixel main camera with a variable aperture. The iPhone Duo lacks a variable aperture, and its main camera performance doesn't match the Pro series.

The iPhone 18 Pro also includes a telephoto lens, which the iPhone Duo lacks.

Regarding software features, each model has exclusive functions:

  • iPhone Duo: Smart Take, Kid Cue, Duo Preview
  • iPhone 18 Pro: Smart Focus Tracking, Pro Controls, Apple Reference Image

The iPhone 18 Pro also exclusively supports external recording in ProRes format at up to 4K 60fps, and comes with a "studio-grade quad-microphone array," 1080p 30fps spatial video recording, spatial photos, ProRes RAW, Genlock, and more.

Battery: All Models Offer Excellent Battery Life

Since the iPhone Duo has two displays, its official battery life varies depending on which screen is being used. Overall, Apple promises excellent battery life for both the Duo and the iPhone 18 Pro.

Here are the figures announced by Apple:

  • iPhone Duo outer screen: up to 44 hours
  • iPhone Duo foldable screen: up to 31 hours
  • iPhone 18 Pro: up to 36 hours
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: up to 45 hours

Everyone's usage habits are different, but if you average the battery life of the iPhone Duo's two screens, the average video playback time is approximately 38 hours.

Other Differences: Face ID, Buttons, Software, Apple Pencil, and More

The authentication methods differ between the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro: the former uses Touch ID, while the latter uses Face ID.

The iPhone Duo doesn't have an Action button, but it does feature Camera Control.

The iPhone Duo has several multitasking advantages in iOS 27, such as support for split-view app usage and a unique landscape display mode. It also adds other interesting software features, such as a half-folded StandBy mode.

The iPhone Duo will support Apple Pencil (USB-C model) later this year, which is another advantage over the iPhone 18 Pro.

Both the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro feature the new C2 modem, but the iPhone 18 Pro Max doesn't include it, which is an intriguing situation.

The iPhone 18 Pro is available in four colors: Burgundy, Glacier, Black, and Silver. The iPhone Duo only comes in two colors: Star White and Night Sky.

Finally, the two devices use different design materials: the iPhone 18 Pro features an aluminum unibody, while the iPhone Duo uses titanium.

Price and Availability: Significant Gaps in Both Areas

Pricing is another major difference between Apple's new models. Here are the starting prices for the 256GB version:

  • iPhone Duo: $1,999
  • iPhone 18 Pro: $1,199
  • iPhone 18 Pro Max: $1,299

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will be available for pre-order this Saturday, with official sales starting next Friday (September 18). The iPhone Duo won't open for pre-orders until October 16, and will ship on October 23.

For more coverage of the Apple launch event, please visit our dedicated news center.
